jobs.occupation: Scientific programmer and data analyst in Environmental Science
jobs.description:
Would you like to apply your programming and data analysis skills to research and environmental advisory work addressing air pollution and climate change? We are looking for a scientific programmer and data analyst to help develop, modernize and operate atmospheric models and analyze complex environmental datasets. You will join the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling at the Department of Environmental Science, Aarhus University, working closely with researchers on both scientific projects and research-based advice to public authorities. 

The Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling conducts research and provides research-based advice on atmospheric processes, emission inventories, air pollution and climate modeling, integrated impact assessment for health, nature and climate, and land-use and remote-sensing research. You will play an important role in advancing this work through the development and improvement of scientific models and the analysis and interpretation of complex environmental data.

This is a permanent position based in Roskilde, Denmark, with an expected starting date of February 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a permanent position starting 1 Feb 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
You will participate in research and advisory projects, the latter mainly for the Danish Ministry of Environment. Both research and advisory projects aim to understand atmospheric processes, helping ministries and environmental agencies regulate air quality and protect our environment. You will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary team of researchers. 

Together with researchers, your main task will be to restructure, improve and modernize existing air quality models and forecast systems as well as to contribute to the development of new integrated air pollution models. A key part of your role will be to help modernize our scientific codebase by introducing and applying good software development practices, making our models and workflows easier to maintain, document, test and reproduce. Your tasks will also include developing and automating workflows for computationally demanding model simulations, including parallel computing, and the processing of large datasets, as well as developing and maintaining applications and scripts in Linux and Windows environments.

You will have the opportunity to collaborate with various research groups and shape the Section’s data science strategy. In addition, you will take part in department-wide initiatives such as workshops, presentations and events related to data science, and contribute to reports and scientific publications.

Your profile
We welcome applications from candidates who meet most, though not necessarily all, of the following qualifications:

 * An MSc or PhD in computer science, software engineering, physics, applied mathematics or a related field
 * Advanced programming skills in languages such as Python, R, Fortran, C/C++ or similar, including experience with scientific computing, data analysis and visualization libraries
 * Experience with implementing and applying modern software development practices for scientific computing, including code organization, version control, documentation, testing, maintainability and reproducibility, as well as experience with parallel computing
 * Experience in handling and analyzing large datasets

We are looking for a curious, proactive and motivated colleague who is keen to develop new technical skills and acquire knowledge of atmospheric and air pollution science. Experience with the development and application of air quality models would be welcome, but is not required.

You should enjoy working both independently and collaboratively, sharing knowledge and providing technical guidance to colleagues. Good communication skills and excellent written and spoken English are important. Danish language skills are an advantage, but not a requirement.

Additional experience in any of the following areas would be an advantage, but is not required:
 * GIS and geospatial data
 * Development and integration of APIs and web-based applications
 * Working with and modernizing legacy scientific software, including Delphi or similar technologies
 * Machine learning and AI methods

About the Department 
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department within the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. Our research covers a wide range of fields, including physics, chemistry, microbiology, social sciences, geography, and environmental economics. The department conducts research and provides research-based advice to ministries and public authorities. Our work addresses major societal challenges such as pollution control, land and water management, climate change, biodiversity protection, and ecosystem services.

We have a highly collaborative work environment, where all employees contribute to securing the research and advisory projects that fund the majority of the department’s activities. We value equality, diversity, and a strong work-life balance.

The Research Group

The selected candidate will join the Atmospheric Modelling Group within the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling. The group focuses on air pollution processes and climate interactions. It develops, tests, and applies models across spatial scales, from global to local, and examines the environmental, health, and socioeconomic impacts of air pollution and climate change. Close collaboration with other sections within the department is essential, particularly in areas such as atmospheric measurements, environmental economics, and geography.

In the group, we specialize in 
 * Atmospheric physics and chemistry, including numerical methods and computer science
 * Air pollution modeling at global, regional (Northern Hemisphere, Europe, Denmark) and local scales (urban areas, point sources)
 * Numerical weather prediction models at different spatial scales
 * Integrated assessment modeling (impact on health, environment, and climate)
 * Environmental noise modeling
 * Climate modeling and its links to air pollution and health
 * Decision-support for policy makers on emissions, air quality, and health impacts

Work location 

The place of work will be at Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located approx. 30 km from Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits. 

International candidates may find information concerning living and working in Denmark at www.workindenmark.dk. AU International Center offers a full range of services to make your transition to Denmark as smooth as possible (http://www.au.dk/en/internationalcentre/ias/), and the department will assist foreign candidates with finding a suitable place to live.

Contact information

Further information may be obtained from Professor Peter Langen, Head of the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling, at plangen@envs.au.dk or +45 2061 8369.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 3 Dec 2026.

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between either the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions, where you will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8, or subject to section 15 of the collective agreement for IT employees (PROSA) in the service of the state and LC/CO10-S (the Confederation of Teachers’ Unions/the Danish Confederation of Public Employees of 2010) collective agreement.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The PhD candidate will, as part of a collaboration project between a private enterprise and DTU Construct, carry out experimental clearance flow research with ammonia and other sustainable marine fuels. 

Pressure and temperature conditions, resembling those in a marine engine booster pump, are created in an in-house designed clearance flow test rig. Measured clearance flow data will be used to develop and validate accurate flow models. The test rig will be further modified to enable testing and evaluation of different sealing solutions.

Responsibilities and qualifications

The PhD candidate will be responsible for continuing our development of a high-pressure ammonia flow rig, conduct test campaigns with different ammonia pump components and develop both theoretical and experimental foundation for developing ammonia compatible sealing techniques.

The candidate should have significant experience with:

• Safe handling of ammonia and other liquified gases in test setups.
• Design and wiring electronic data acquisition and control systems using PC Schematics.
• LabView programming.
• Mechanical design and FEM analysis using Solid Works.
• Data processing of large experimental sets of dynamic flow and pressure data using statistical methods in Matlab.
• CMM (Coordinate Measurement Machine) measurement and preferably have experience with Calypso Software.
• Data processing large complex geometric data sets from CMM measurements for 3-dimensional analysis of tested pump components.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

jobs.occupation: GLP QA professional
jobs.description:
**Your impact begins here

**As GLP QA Professional, you will help make sure non-clinical research at Novo is carried out to Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards. You will oversee studies, inspect internal and external work, and turn what you see into clear, practical recommendations that keep research reliable and moving. You will shape how quality is built into non-clinical processes, strengthening the foundation for treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases.

**What You’ll Bring

**You bring a balanced, practical quality mindset. You work systematically and independently, take initiative and stay flexible when priorities change. To succeed in this role, you have:

• Experience as a laboratory technician and relevant qualification, or a master’s degree in science, pharmacy, medicine or a similar field.

• Experience within GLP, for example from quality assurance, GLP-regulated work, non-clinical research or laboratory activities.

• Knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS) and the ability to interpret and communicate regulatory and procedural requirements.

• Strong analytical and organisational skills, with attention to detail and the ability to work systematically and independently.

• Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to build constructive relationships with internal colleagues and external Contract Research Organisations (CROs).

• Proficiency in written and spoken English, and confidence in communicating observations, recommendations and quality matters.

**Desirable, But Not Essential

**Experience from industrial drug development.

**What You’ll Do

**You will be the quality partner for GLP-regulated activities, helping colleagues and CROs meet requirements while keeping study quality and compliance protected.

• Perform quality oversight and compliance verification of GLP-regulated activities, including review of study plans, reports, relevant SOPs and documentation from internal areas and external CROs.

• Plan and conduct study-based and process-based internal inspections, including Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP) activities where relevant.

• Support stakeholders on GLP requirements and general quality matters, including review of GLP action plans from internal and external audits.

• Contribute to maintaining and improving the department’s QMS, including harmonisation, digitalisation and simplification initiatives.

• Communicate observations, regulatory requirements and practical quality recommendations clearly to internal and external stakeholders, and take part in relevant projects, audits and regulatory inspections.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Non-Clinical Quality, a diverse team of 15 skilled colleagues in Søborg. It is one of two sister departments within Process Management, Non-Clinical, IT & AI Quality, part of R&D Quality. In R&D, curiosity, data, collaboration and operational excellence come together to advance scientific ideas towards clinical testing, and Non-Clinical Quality helps make sure the processes behind that work are fit for purpose.

The team provides QMS expertise to a global organisation and works closely with stakeholders across the value chain. You will have many interfaces: research and laboratory colleagues in internal areas, external CROs and other collaboration partners, and teams across the organisation working on improvement projects.

You will work in an international environment where clear communication helps you build trust, create clarity around requirements and keep work moving. Some travel may be required for audits and other GLP QA activities.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will build your GLP expertise and take on increasing responsibility, with room to influence how quality is embedded in non-clinical research processes. Alongside day-to-day oversight, you will contribute to cross-organisational improvement projects and share ideas that improve methods, systems and processes.

You will be supported to perform at your best, trusted to work independently and encouraged to make your voice heard. You will grow through practical experience, close collaboration with colleagues and continuous learning.

838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

jobs.occupation: Clinical Research Associate
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about clinical research and eager to make a significant impact in the world of drug development? NBCD is seeking a dedicated Clinical Research Associate (CRA) to join our dynamic team at the forefront of international drug development research. Join us in an environment fueled by dedication and inspired by our core values: "Team up, Take on, and Try out." Here, you'll have the chance to make a significant difference while expanding your skillset.

Who are we?

NBCD, a key part of the Sanos Group with around 245 employees, is a world-leading CRO specializing in osteoarthritis and musculoskeletal diseases. We provide top-tier scientific and clinical trial services to the biotech and pharmaceutical industries. At NBCD, innovation is at our core, enabling us to develop life-changing medications efficiently through pioneering study designs and flawless execution. We focus on a few therapeutic areas, letting science drive our business, particularly in connective tissue diseases like osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. Our comprehensive support covers everything from study design to regulatory affairs, ensuring expert handling at every step. Renowned worldwide for our scientific and operational excellence, NBCD leads in international medication development.

Your key role and responsibilities

Your role will be highly varied and include the following responsibilities:

• You will conduct on-site monitoring of NBCD trials according to ICH-GCP, which involves regular visits to hospitals and clinics in Denmark and other countries to:

• Ensure patient rights and safety are protected, and that physicians conduct trials according to protocols, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and approved procedures.

• Verify that electronically reported data is accurate, complete, and matches source data in patient files.

• Educate site staff and provide guidance on study-related matters.

• Write visit reports and follow-up letters to investigators.

NBCD has pioneered Risk-Based Monitoring, and you will play a critical role in Centralized Monitoring, a major part of this process. This includes:

• Remotely reviewing clinical database entries at our Søborg office to ensure data quality by proactively identifying issues, analyzing trends, and querying investigators for appropriate actions.

• Documenting findings and actions in centralized monitoring reports.

• Ensuring the Centralized Monitoring approach effectively identifies issues remotely.

Additionally, you will have the opportunity to work closely with our Clinical Trial Managers (CTM), assist them and gain responsibility for various tasks related to study or vendor management. These tasks can be tailored to your skills and interests.

Desired skills and experience

We are looking for candidates with an educational degree in health sciences who have experience with good clinical practice and clinical trials, whether through university projects or previous positions. Excellent communication skills are essential, and since most of our communication is in English, fluency in business English, both oral and written, is required.

Additionally, as the role involves on-site monitoring at Danish investigational sites, we prefer candidates who speak Danish natively or fluently.

Personal profile

You excel at working independently and take full accountability for your responsibilities. With a keen eye for detail, you understand that study monitoring relies on the accurate and thorough review of patient files and supporting documents. You are dedicated to meeting deadlines and following through on commitments, working persistently and with self-motivation.

You are committed to fostering a positive work environment where colleagues can thrive. You approach challenges with a solution-oriented mindset, maintaining a positive and optimistic outlook that encourages collaboration and respects individualism.

You are comfortable with broad responsibilities, as we value agility and efficiency, and believe in empowering our employees with the freedom to operate and innovate. Your enthusiasm for innovative research drives your desire to learn new approaches and expand your core skill set.

Additionally, you are willing and able to travel both within Denmark and internationally, as our CRAs also monitor sites in English-speaking countries such as the UK and USA.

Are we the right cultural fit for you?

Our commitment to you is encapsulated in our promise to every one of our employees saying ‘Trust in you - in your development and impact´.

This pledge extends uniformly across all entities within the Sanos Group organization, including NBCD, ensuring that you feel its effects from the very offset of your interaction.

If you are curious about whether you would thrive within the Sanos Group culture and the Sanos Way of Leading, reflect on whether you see yourself working within our principles:

• Take on - Responsibility is given, and we inspire you to take it.

• Try out - Explore diverse tasks and grow professionally.

• Team up - We don’t just work together; we thrive together.

Want to know more? Check out the Voice of NBCD people here.

Apply and make a real impact

We look forward to hearing from you, so please send your application through the “apply” link.

We will be performing interviews ongoing in the process and look to fill the position as soon as possible. We close the position when we find the right candidate.

For further information about the role please contact, Associate Director, Anne Andresen, anne@nbcd.com.

You will be office-based at our headquarters in Søborg and you will be required to travel on a regular basis to our clinical sites within Denmark and other countries.

If you proceed in the recruitment process, you will go through a few additional steps where both you and we will assess whether this position is the right match for both parties. As part of the recruitment process, we use assessments to ensure the optimal match and the best foundation for future collaboration.

NBCD is dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives leads to better decision-making and innovation. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive.

jobs.occupation: Professor / Associate Professor / Senior Researcher taking lead in Catchment and Freshwater Ecosystem sciences
jobs.description:
Are you an engaged, leading scientist of international standing, with deep expertise in the research of catchments and freshwater ecosystems, and excellent science leadership skills? Do you have the scientific vision to guide the strategic direction for a nationally and internationally recognized research community working with catchments, wetlands, lakes, streams and nature-based solutions?

The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a full-time permanent scientific position (Full Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Researcher) in the Catchment science and Freshwater Ecology (CaFE) focus area. We are looking for a scientist who enjoys taking lead and working strategically with organizational impact covering the range of research areas in CaFE.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a permanent position from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.

Job description
The position centers around research and research based advisory in catchment processes and freshwater ecosystems – including wetlands, streams and lakes and the landscapes like forests, agricultural areas etc. that surround them. We expect the candidates to have expertise and track record with one or more of the key thematic areas:

• Hydrology and the retention and transport of nutrients and hazardous substances
• Biogeochemical processes and emissions of greenhouse gases from land and water bodies, including interactions with carbon and nutrient dynamics 
• Freshwater ecology and the links between abiotic and biotic processes, including ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, and responses to human pressures and climate change
• Nature-based solutions and ecosystem restoration to strengthen biodiversity and resilience and reduce nutrient loss, limit greenhouse gas emissions and regulate water flow in the landscape
• Combining long-term monitoring data with novel research using laboratory, mesocosm and field experiments, in situ sensor data and catchment- and ecosystem modelling
At Department of Ecoscience, all scientific staff in general are expected to contribute to external income generation, dissemination of knowledge, and talent development. Your specific scientific responsibilities may also include:

• Taking the lead on the development and implementation of the CaFE focus area strategy as part of the Department’s strategy, Ecoscience 2030 – including formulating concrete goals and action plans for implementation in dialogue with colleagues and the Department’s management
• Setting the direction and fostering a strong and inclusive research environment across the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions
• Bringing our research and knowledge to Danish ministries and agencies as well as to other relevant national, European and international decision makers through science-based advice, making an impact for the society around us
• Promoting innovation within the focus area and wider department by fostering use of new and/or novel technologies through closer dialogue and interaction with other sections/focus area within the department and across the faculty
• Supporting the scientific development and career paths of colleagues in the focus area
Your profile
We are looking for a scientist with a strong research track record as well as documented experience with science-based advisory work and leadership of research staff. You have expertise within catchment science and freshwater ecology, previous experience working in interdisciplinary teams and from broad sectoral collaborations. Applicants must hold a PhD in hydrology, limnology, freshwater ecology, biogeochemistry, environmental science, physical geography, environmental engineering or a closely related discipline. The level of appointment (Full Professor, Associate Professor or Senior Researcher) will be determined based on qualifications.
We value in particular:

• Excellent leadership experience from similar research environments; e.g., leading larger research groups and taking responsibility for strategic development of larger units (academic citizenship)
• Skills in strategic scientific coordination, strategy development, project management, and building research networks
• An established international network, collaborative skills and relationships within catchment science and/or freshwater ecology and nature-based solutions
• Documented experience in securing and leading externally funded research projects
• Documented experience with science-based advisory work and engagement with authorities and other stakeholders
Excellent written and spoken English; Strong Danish language skills are an advantage.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience, with approximately 300 employees in Aarhus and Roskilde, is one of Denmark's leading research environments in applied ecology, spanning terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and Arctic ecosystems. We conduct both fundamental and applied research and deliver Science-based advisory services to authorities in Denmark and Greenland. Our work is grounded in long-term monitoring, field-based data collection, and advanced modelling, and we pride ourselves on a research culture characterized by high scientific integrity, strong interdisciplinary collaboration, and societal relevance. Our values are impact, professionalism, curiosity, collaboration and trust.

CaFE is the department's focus area for catchment science and freshwater ecology, integrating the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions. We are around 80 research and technical employees working to generate the data and knowledge that qualify decision-making on conservation and recovery of deteriorated wetlands and inland waters. Our vision is to maintain and expand our position as the key national focal point for applied research and modelling within catchment processes and freshwater ecosystem dynamics, helping authorities monitor, manage and mitigate human impacts on wetlands and freshwaters.

We combine long-term monitoring data with experimental approaches and modelling, and we have the strongest national scientific environment within modelling of nutrient transport, biogeochemical processes in wetlands, experimental freshwater ecology, lake ecosystem modelling and lake restoration. Key infrastructure includes a series of living labs in constructed wetlands, lakes, ponds and streams, including the semi-field mesocosm lake experiments at Lemming that have been running for more than 30 years.

Find out more about our current strategy, departmental values and more here: https://ecos.au.dk/en/about-us/au-ecoscience-our-strategy

What we offer
• A full-time permanent scientific position with an internationally competitive research environment and access to unique long-term datasets and world-class field and semi-field infrastructure
• A central role in shaping the scientific direction of CaFE, contributing actively to the focus area strategy under Ecoscience 2030 and beyond
• An interdisciplinary and dynamic working environment across catchment, freshwater, terrestrial, marine and Arctic research
• Highly engaged, motivated and positive colleagues and an innovative and dynamic working environment, where culture and values are important
• A working environment characterized by high scientific standards, trust, and well-being
• Close, trust-based relationships with Danish ministries and agencies and strong national and international research networks
• Access to professional support for international researchers and their families relocating to Denmark
For candidates with the right qualifications and experience in strategic research leadership, a temporary role as Deputy Head of Department with responsibility for the CaFE focus area of the Department of Ecoscience will be possible. This role includes participation in the Department’s management group. Further education/competence building in leadership will be offered. Contact the Head of Department (details below) for a more detailed description of this role.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is AU Campus Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information about the position, please contact Head of Department Mikkel Tamstorf (mpt@ecos.au.dk; +45 53 57 50 44).

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) has a leading position in research related to breeding for sustainability related traits in dairy cattle such as feed- and nitrogen efficiency, resilience, and methane emissions. This is enabled by an ambitious farm based infrastructure with large scale measurement of methane emissions, feed intake, feed and environment parameters, productivity, and novel phenotypes on individual cows, based on collaboration with industry and international researchers. The successful candidate for these positions will join our team to further advance in the areas of feed- and nitrogen efficiency, resilience, and methane. This includes phenotype definition, genotype by environment studies, variance component estimation, and integrating novel genetically related traits using digital tools or functional genomic information or OMICS to improve genomic prediction models. The successful candidate will collaborate with industry partners, support teaching at undergraduate and graduate levels, and co-supervise Master's, and PhD students. The candidate is expected to help with creating a collaborative work environment within and outside QGG that integrates novel innovative research programs towards the green transition in animal agriculture.

The position is a full-time position for a period of 2 years, starting on 1 March 2027. There are possibilities for extension to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and funding is available. If your research profile does not completely match the descriptions above but you have a theoretical background and are interested in developing one of the research areas mentioned, QGG would like to hear your motivation for seeking this position.

The position offers you:
• Contribute to ongoing projects in the area of feed- and nitrogen efficiency, resilience, and methane
• Advance the genetic modeling of these traits, including genotype by environment interactions, and OMICS
• Participate in project applications
• Collaborate with diverse group of researchers nationally and internationally
• Engage with commercial breeding organizations
• Publish high-quality research in peer-reviewed journals and at conferences
• Support in teaching, and (co-)supervise BSc, MSc and PhD students – though teaching duties may be low
 

The ideal candidate:
• Holds a PhD with a strong background in quantitative genetics and/or animal breeding
• Has published high-quality research in peer-reviewed journals
• Experience with one or more scripting language (e.g., R, Python, Julia) and/or genetic software (e.g., DMU, ASReml)
• Can biologically interpret results and relate to breeding decision making
• Exhibits excellent teamwork skills and has experience collaborating with scientists across different disciplines nationally and internationally
• Possesses effective communication skills and can communicate complex scientific concepts to diverse audiences, whether in academia, industry, or society.
• Shows interest in teaching and mentoring of BSc, MSc and PhD-students

Who we are:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a vibrant and exciting interdisciplinary center for research and education in quantitative genetics and quantitative genomics (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). QGG is an international organization with more than 70 employees and visiting researchers from more than 20 countries. We perform basic and applied research within plant, livestock and human quantitative genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and precision medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. QGG is located at the central campus in Aarhus and at the AU Flakkebjerg campus in newly renovated offices with well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, equipment, and highperforming computing clusters.

Place of work:

The Department of Forensic Medicine at Faculty of Health Sciences at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in the field of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology as per 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a permanent full time position.

As associate professor at the Department of Forensic Medicine, you will be part of a workplace with dedicated and specialised employees. The shared goal of our employees is to prevent and solve crimes, accidents, premature deaths and suicides through research, education and forensic examinations. The department is part of the Faculty of Health at Aarhus University with a permanent staff of seventy employees who work in two departments delivering impartial and evidence-based public sector consultancy for the danish police. The Section of Forensic Chemistry identifies and determines the purity of drugs in both biological material and illicit drugs seized by the police. The Section of Forensic Pathology and clinical forensic medicine performs forensic autopsies, crime scene investigations and clinical forensic examinations. Both departments hold either ISO 17025 or ISO 17020 quality standard accreditations. In addition to the two sections, the department has three research units which focus on bioanalytical chemistry, forensic imaging and clinical forensic medicine. The employees work in an interface between public sector consultancy and basic and applied research, and the department has particular focus on the good work environment, as this is a prerequisite for high quality in the performance of tasks at all levels. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your job responsibilities
As Associate Professor of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology, you will contribute to the department’s research, teaching environment and commissioned work, and to the university’s overall strategy. You will contribute to the development of the department both individually and in collaboration with others via your research of high international quality. You will furthermore contribute to the development of the department’s commissioned work within your area of expertise. You possess professional collaborative skills and a broad academic network across disciplines and institutions, which you are able to bring into play in your contribution to the academic development of Aarhus University and its profile both locally, nationally and internationally. 

Your main tasks will consist of:

• Commissioned work within the field of Forensic Anthropology
• Research of high international quality, including publication in top international journals and communicating your research in national and international academic networks.
• Teaching, supervision and examination of Bachelor’s and Master's degree students, as well as supervision of PhD students.
• Grant application to attract external research funding.
• Collaboration with relevant research environments across departments at Health, and with relevant national and international research environments.
• Involvement in assessment and committee work at Aarhus University.
• Dissemination of your research to the outside world.
• Contributing to the development of the faculty's PhD courses and new teaching activities

Your main teaching and research tasks, as listed above, may be conducted in affiliation with the Department of Molecular Medicine, Department of Clinical Medicine.

You will report to the Head of Department, Christian Lindholst, on matters relating to research and teaching, and to the Head of the Section of Forensic Pathology, Professor Lene Warner Boel, on matters relating to commissioned work.

Your competences 
You have established yourself as a prominent researcher within molecular bone histology and you possess documented solid research and teaching qualifications at a high international level. You have broad international cooperative partnerships, a documented ability to establish research collaboration across disciplinary and institutional boundaries, and experience of research partnerships with private and public-sector stakeholders, and you have potential of becoming a skilled group leader. At the same time, you have experience with grant writing to national and international funding bodies. We also draw attention to a stay or employment at at least one internationally recognised research institution. Finally, it is essential that you possess knowledge about forensic anthropological examinations, enabling you to actively contribute to the daily casework and develop the future of commissioned work within your area of expertise.

As a person, you are dedicated and a skilled communicator. You are able to build relationships based on trust with students, colleagues and partners. As a lecturer you communicate the newest and relevant knowledge in a committed, clear and comprehensible manner. As a supervisor you are professional, inspiring and inclusive.

You are ready to take co-responsibility for the development of the department's research, education and commissioned work at the highest international level and for ensuring that we maintain a good work environment. You naturally involve yourself in interdisciplinary collaboration at departmental, faculty and university level as well as nationally and internationally.

We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English. International applicants are expected to learn Danish, and Aarhus University arranges Danish teaching. 

In order to be assessed as qualified for an Associate Professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be used.

Obtaining a child certificate is a prerequisite for employment in the position.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Head of Department Christian Lindholst tel.: (+45) 8716 7500

Your place of work will be the Department of Forensic Medicine, Palle Juul-Jensen’s Boulevard 43, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark. Teaching and research activities may also be conducted at Department of Molecular Medicine, Department of Clinical Medicine, Brendstrupgårdsvej 21A, 8200 Aarhus N.

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Strategy & Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Job Title: Senior Director, Strategy & Corporate Development

Location: Brøndby, Denmark

Working model: Hybrid

Make an impact with us

At Milestone Systems, what you do matters. People are at the heart of everything we do, grounded in integrity, collaboration, strong relationships, and a curiosity that drives continuous learning. It is how we work together, learn from one another, embrace new perspectives, and create lasting impact.

In this role, you will help shape Milestone’s strategic direction and, equally importantly, turn strategy into action. You will lead our Strategy & Corporate Development team and work closely with senior leaders across the organization to drive some of our most important strategic and transformational priorities.

About the role

As Senior Director, Strategy & Corporate Development, you will lead Milestone’s work across corporate strategy, strategy execution, corporate development, strategic transformation, and global market and competitive intelligence.

You will work closely with the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), Senior Leadership Team (SLT), and leaders across the business to develop our strategic direction, provide insights that support key business decisions, and drive strategic and transformational priorities across the organization.

You will report to the EVP, Strategy, Communications & Brand.

What makes this role particularly interesting is the combination of strategy, insight, transformation and execution. You will not only help define where Milestone is going, but also play a central role in mobilizing the organization around our priorities and driving the strategic initiatives and transformations that will get us there.

What you will do

• Lead Milestone’s corporate strategy development and the translation of strategy into clear priorities and execution.

• Drive selected strategic and transformational initiatives across the organization, creating alignment, structure and momentum from ambition through execution.

• Lead and develop a team of Strategy Managers and Market & Competitive Intelligence Managers, building strong capabilities across strategy, insights and execution.

• Own our global market and competitive intelligence agenda, ensuring leaders have relevant insights in-to markets, customers, competitors and industry developments to support strategic decision-making.

• Drive the strategic and commercial aspects of M&A, including assessing strategic relevance and fit, evaluating opportunities and leading commercial due diligence.

• Partner closely with ELT, SLT and functional leaders on strategic questions, transformation priorities, business opportunities and key decisions.

• Strengthen Milestone’s ability to turn strategic choices into action, helping leadership navigate com-plex, cross-functional change and maintain focus on the outcomes that matter most.

What you bring

We are looking for someone with:

• 5+ years of top-tier management consulting experience, ideally within strategy, transformation, corporate development or related areas.

• Strong business acumen and the ability to understand complex markets, competitive dynamics and business models.

• Experience leading complex strategic or transformational initiatives across an organization and bringing different functions and stakeholders together around a common outcome.

• Experience with M&A and corporate development, particularly strategic assessment and commercial due diligence.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with the ability to turn complex information into clear recommendations and decisions.

• Proven leadership experience and the ability to develop and lead a team of experienced professionals.

• The confidence and credibility to work closely with senior executives while building strong relationships across different functions and levels of the organization.

How you will make a difference

You combine strategic thinking with a strong drive to make things happen. You are comfortable moving between big-picture questions and hands-on problem solving, and you know when further analysis adds value and when it is time to make a decision and move forward.

You are naturally collaborative, but also able to challenge thinking, bring an independent point of view and create clarity when questions are complex or ambiguous.

Meet the team

You’ll lead the Strategy & Corporate Development team, bringing together strategy, market and competitive intelligence, corporate development, and the leadership of key strategic initiatives. The team works across the organization and closely with senior leadership. We value curiosity, sharp analysis, collaboration and, importantly, the ability to turn strategic choices into tangible progress.

How we support you

At Milestone, we want you to have the opportunity to do meaningful work, develop your skills and grow your career.

• Individual development plans aligned with your career goals

• Access to training, learning resources, and certifications

• Flexible working arrangements

• Supportive leadership and regular feedback

• Opportunities for cross-functional and cross-regional collaboration

• Social activities and spaces to connect with colleagues

Ready to make an impact?

If you’re excited about shaping strategy, turning it into action and driving some of the most important strategic and transformational priorities across a global organization, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and submit your CV in English.

About Milestone Systems

Milestone Systems is a leading provider of data-driven video technology software. Our portfolio includes XProtect video management software, Arcules video surveillance as a service, and BriefCam analytics. We amplify what organizations of any size can see, do, and achieve with video.

jobs.occupation: Operative Business Specialist
jobs.description:
Join IBSA Nordic as Operative Business Specialist and play a key role in operational support and commercial execution within the Dermo Aesthetics business.

Turn ideas into value-creating customer and business-driving initiatives

Reporting to the Nordic Marketing Manager, Mette Busk, you will join the Nordic commercial team in Copenhagen and act as a commercial enabler and project lead, generating ideas and leading key projects with targeted accounts, customer engagement initiatives, and events across the Nordic region, with a strong focus on IBSA’s VALUANCE (Value Through Alliance) concept. You will develop and drive VALU drive VALUANCE projects with selected Nordic accounts based on segmentation, customer needs, and sales potential in close collaboration with Regional Managers. You will engage directly with customers and co-own selected key accounts from proposal through execution and follow-up. The role also includes planning and executing events, business webinars, and other customer activities, as well as coordinating trade fairs, congresses, and PR activities with the sales and marketing team. In addition, you will conduct and coordinate market research and competitor analyses across the Nordic markets to support commercial decisions and contribute to the development and adaptation of customer-facing marketing materials. Across projects, you will ensure strong operational follow-up and stakeholder coordination. Approximately 60–65 field and travel days per year are expected.

Coordinator with a commercial mindset and strong execution skills

We imagine that you bring experience from a customer-facing commercial role within sales and/or, marketing, event management, or business development, from the pharmaceutical, medtech, healthcare, aesthetics, or life sciences sectors. Accustomed to coordinating multiple projects and stakeholders, you combine commercial understanding, event execution capabilities, sales experience, and solid cross-functional coordination skills. Experience with events, webinars, congresses, trade fairs, or other customer engagement activities is highly relevant. Strong interpersonal skills enable you to communicate fluently in English and one Nordic language, both written and spoken.

To succeed in this role, you are structured, proactive, and self-driven, with a strong focus on execution and attention to detail. Furthermore, you are relationship-driven, take ownership, move initiatives forward, and thrive in a dynamic Nordic environment.

Turn ideas into impact across the Nordics

This is your opportunity to combine commercial thinking with hands-on execution, work closely with customers and colleagues across the Nordics and contribute to the continued development of IBSA Nordic’s Dermo Aesthetics business. The recruitment process is carried out by Venaris Executive Search (www.venaris.dk). For more information regarding the position, please reach out to Executive Search Consultant Lærke Christensen on lc@venaris.dk. All requests will be handled confidentially. If this position is for you, do not hesitate to apply by uploading your CV in PDF format – it is not necessary to include a cover letter.

IBSA Nordic

Established in 2014, IBSA Nordic ApS is part of the international IBSA Group and has built a strong Nordic organization with headquarters in Copenhagen, comprising 35 employees across Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, and the Baltic countries, working with the commercialization of pharmaceutical and dermo aesthetic products. Joining IBSA Nordic means becoming part of a cross-cultural organization where collaboration, learning, and development are a natural part of everyday work.

jobs.occupation: Product Manager – Drives (Sønderborg, Denmark)
jobs.description:
At OJ Electronics, we’re looking for a Product Manager to join our Drives team and play an important role in the continued development of our Drives business with a strong focus on drive solutions for cooling and compressor applications. You’ll combine technical and commercial product responsibility with close collaboration across sales, R&D, supply chain, and customers – all with the aim of keeping our drive solutions competitive.

OJ Electronics – a Danish producer of HVAC drives, AHU controllers, and thermostats for electric floor heating – is looking for a product manager to join our Drives organization in Sønderborg, Denmark.

The position centers on selected drive solutions within the OJ portfolio. Responsibilities range from roadmap planning, customer adaptations, and product follow-up to release coordination, quality assurance, and second-level support for selected customers and applications.

The role is part of a dynamic organization with a high level of collaboration across product management, sales, and development functions. For the right candidate, it offers the opportunity to contribute directly to a fast-growing business area where decisions, priorities, and product improvements quickly become visible in the market.

Your role

At OJ, you’ll help coordinate the ongoing development and support of our drive products and applications, ensuring alignment between technical development, commercial priorities, and customer needs.

Your specific responsibilities will include:

• Managing drive solutions for compressor and cooling applications

• Supporting completion and follow-up of drive projects

• Developing and maintaining product roadmaps and release plans

• Following up on quality issues and supporting corrective actions

• Providing second-level support for selected customers and applications

• Working closely with R&D, sales, and supply chain to ensure focus and progress

• Supporting work related to product specifications, business cases, and market analysis

Must-have qualifications

• Technical background within cooling applications, drives, power electronics, or related systems

• Commercial understanding and interest in market-driven product development

• Experience from product management, business development, or a similar role in a B2B environment

• Strong coordination and planning skills

• Experience working with product roadmaps, specifications, or release planning

• Structured and collaborative working style

• Strong communication skills in both Danish and English, written and spoken

Nice-to-have qualifications

• Experience with market and competitor analysis

• Familiarity with drives, or industrial control systems

• German language skills

• Experience working across technical and commercial functions

Working at OJ

At OJ Electronics, you’ll find an informal, open and collaborative culture where people take pride in doing quality work.

We offer:

• A flat organisational structure where decisions are made quickly

• Opportunities to grow your expertise and responsibility over time

• A healthy work-life balance and flexible working hours

• Competitive salary and pension package

• A modern workplace with canteen and good facilities

Employee satisfaction has consistently remained above 80 for several years – and we take pride in maintaining a workplace where people truly thrive.

Please note that this position is based in Sønderborg, Denmark, and requires your physical presence on site. This is not a hybrid or remote position.

The application process

For this position, we will be interviewing on an ongoing basis until we find the right person.

About OJ Electronics

Founded in 1964 and headquartered in Sønderborg, Denmark, OJ Electronics produces HVAC drives, AHU controllers, and underfloor heating thermostats. Our products are available through partners and distributors worldwide, and we have subsidiaries and sales offices in key markets, including the United States and Poland. Everywhere, we are known for our innovative approach, insistence on product quality, and deep application knowledge – all of which helps customers differentiate themselves in the market.

In June 2023, OJ Electronics was acquired by BITZER Electronics, a BITZER Group company also headquartered in Sønderborg. This makes OJ Electronics part of the BITZER Group family, which is represented at 75 locations in over 40 countries and employs some 4500 people worldwide, including about 185 at OJ Electronics.
